title: Comparison of Vibratome and Compresstome Sectioning for Immunofluorescence Staining
author: Abdelaal, Kim, et al.
materials: In situ tetramer staining combined with immunohistochemistry was done as previously described [5,9,25]. Biotinylated molecules of Mamu-A1*001:01 loaded with SIV Gag (181– 189) CTPYDINQM (CM9) peptides (will be referred to as Mamu-A1/Gag hereafter) and of Mamu-A1 loaded with an irrelevant peptide FLPSDYFPSV (FLP) from the hepatitis-B viral protein (served as a negative control) were obtained from the NIH Tetramer Core Facility. MHC tetramers were prepared as previously described [9], by mixing MHC monomers with 6 aliquots of FITC-labeled Extra Avidin (Sigma, St. Louis, MO) over 8 hours to a final molar ratio of 1:4.5. For in situ tetramer and antibody staining, fresh tissue sections were incubated at 4C overnight with MHC class I tetramers (0.5 ug/ml) in 1 ml of PBS containing 100mg/ml heparin (PBS-H) with 2% normal goat serum (NGS). Sections were then washed with chilled PBS-H followed by fixation with freshly prepared 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 hours at RT and washed with chilled PBS-H. For antigen retrieval, sections were boiled 3 times in urea and permeabilized and blocked with PBS-H containing 0.3% triton x-100 0.3% and 2% NGS for 1 hour prior to secondary incubation. A secondary incubation was done overnight at 4°C with rabbit anti-FITC antibodies (BioDesign, New York, NY) diluted 1:10,000, rat-anti-human CD3 antibodies (AbD Serotec clone CD3-12, Raleigh, NC) diluted 1:200, and mouse anti-CD20 antibody clone L26, diluted 1:200 (Novocastra, Leica Microsystems Inc., Buffalo Grobe, IL) in PBS-H containing 2% NGS on rocking platform. Tissue sections were then washed with chilled PBS-H and incubated with Cy3-conjugated goat anti-rabbit antibodies diluted 1:5000 (Jackson ImmunoResearch, West Grove, PA), Cy5-conjugated anti-rat antibody (Jackson ImmunoResearch, West Grove, PA), diluted 1:2000, and Alexa 488-conjugated goat anti-mouse antibody (Molecular Probes, Eugene, OR) diluted 1:2000 in blocking solution for 1–3 days. After the final antibody incubation, tissue sections were washed with PBS-H and post-fixed for 1 hour with 4% paraformaldehyde. Sections were then washed with PBS-H and mounted on slides with warm glycerol gelatin (Sigma, St. Louis, MO) containing 4-mg/ml n-propylgallate (as a fluorophore preservative).

steps.title: Collect and chill tissues
steps.instruction: Euthanize adult female Indian rhesus macaques, dissect fresh genital (vagina, cervix, uterus, ovary) and lymphoid (axillary, mesenteric, inguinal lymph nodes, spleen) tissues, place each tissue piece into tubes containing chilled RPMI supplemented with 100 mg ml⁻¹ heparin, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Ship tissues on ice
steps.instruction: Ship the heparin‑containing tubes on ice overnight to the University of Minnesota.

steps.title: Prepare Vibratome sectioning
steps.instruction: Section fresh unfixed tissue with a Vibratome 3000 following the steps below.

substeps.instruction: Cut each tissue piece with a surgical scalpel into ~0.5 cm × 0.5 cm blocks.
Place blocks in a weigh boat and cover with melted 4 % PBS‑buffered low‑melt agarose kept at 40 °C; allow agarose to solidify on ice.
Fill the Vibratome bath with ice‑cold sterile PBS containing 100 mg ml⁻¹ heparin (PBS‑H).
Insert a half of a double‑edge razor blade (Persona Super Blade, American Safety Razor Co.) into the blade holder and set blade angle to 27°.
Maintain the bath temperature at 0–2 °C using ice or dry ice around the bath chamber.
Glue the solidified agarose block to a metal mounting block with Loctite® 404® Quick‑Set Instant Adhesive (Henkel).
Submerge the mounted block in the PBS‑H bath and cut 200 µm thick sections while the block remains chilled.
Collect individual sections with a fine brush and transfer them to a 24‑well plate for downstream staining.

steps.title: Prepare Compresstome sectioning
steps.instruction: Section fresh unfixed tissue with a Compresstome VF‑300 following the steps below.

substeps.instruction: Cut each tissue piece with a surgical scalpel into ~0.8 cm × 0.8 cm blocks.
Glue each block onto the cutting plunger of a specimen syringe using Loctite® 404® Quick‑Set Instant Adhesive.
Pull the tissue down into the plunger and cover with melted ~40 °C PBS‑H‑buffered low‑melt agarose; place the plunger in a chilled block so the agarose solidifies.
Glue a half of a double‑edge razor blade to the blade holder with Loctite Instant Adhesive and attach it to the Compresstome.
Insert the agarose‑embedded plunger into the Compresstome cutting chamber.
Fill the buffer tank with chilled PBS‑H and add three frozen PBS‑H cubes to maintain ~0 °C.
Align the blade edge to the outlet of the specimen syringe, set section thickness to 200 µm, and start the instrument to cut automatically.
Harvest sections from the buffer chamber with a brush and place them into a 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Prepare MHC tetramers
steps.instruction: Mix MHC monomers with six aliquots of FITC‑labeled Extra Avidin (Sigma) and incubate for 8 h at room temperature to achieve a final molar ratio of 1 : 4.5, generating biotinylated Mamu‑A1/Gag (CM9) tetramers and FLP control tetramers.

steps.title: Tetramer incubation (primary staining)
steps.instruction: Incubate each 200 µm tissue section overnight at 4 °C in 1 ml PBS‑H containing 0.5 µg ml⁻¹ tetramer and 2 % normal goat serum (NGS).

steps.title: Wash after primary incubation
steps.instruction: Wash sections with chilled PBS‑H (3 × 5 min).

steps.title: Fix primary‑stained sections
steps.instruction: Fix sections with freshly prepared 4 % paraformaldehyde for 2 h at room temperature, then wash with chilled PBS‑H.

steps.title: Antigen retrieval and permeabilization
steps.instruction: Boil sections three times in urea (concentration as used in the original protocol), then permeabilize and block by incubating in PBS‑H containing 0.3 % Triton X‑100 and 2 % NGS for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate sections overnight at 4 °C on a rocking platform in PBS‑H with 2 % NGS containing:

substeps.instruction: Rabbit anti‑FITC (BioDesign) diluted 1 : 10 000
Rat anti‑human CD3 (AbD Serotec clone CD3‑12) diluted 1 : 200
Mouse anti‑CD20 (clone L26, Novocastra) diluted 1 : 200

steps.title: Wash after secondary incubation
steps.instruction: Wash sections with chilled PBS‑H (3 × 5 min).

steps.title: Tertiary (fluorophore) antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate sections for 1–3 days at 4 °C in blocking solution containing:

substeps.instruction: Cy3‑conjugated goat anti‑rabbit (Jackson ImmunoResearch) diluted 1 : 5 000
Cy5‑conjugated goat anti‑rat (Jackson ImmunoResearch) diluted 1 : 2 000
Alexa 488‑conjugated goat anti‑mouse (Molecular Probes) diluted 1 : 2 000

steps.title: Post‑fixation
steps.instruction: Post‑fix sections with 4 % paraformaldehyde for 1 h at room temperature, then wash with PBS‑H.

steps.title: Mount sections
steps.instruction: Mount sections on glass slides using warm glycerol gelatin (Sigma) containing 4 mg ml⁻¹ n‑propyl gallate as a fluorophore preservative.

steps.title: Confocal imaging
steps.instruction: Acquire confocal images on an Olympus FluoView 1000 microscope using a 20× objective and 3 µm z‑steps. Begin collection ~6 µm below the tissue surface and continue to a depth of 36–42 µm. Create montage images of multiple 800 × 800 pixel, 200× Z‑scans using Olympus FluoView Viewer software.

steps.title: Record instrument performance metrics
steps.instruction: Document the following comparative data: Compresstome cutting speed ≈5 sections min⁻¹ versus Vibratome ≈0.8 sections min⁻¹ (≈5‑fold faster); maximum section area ≈0.64 cm² (Compresstome) versus ≈0.25 cm² (Vibratome); presence of light source (Vibratome yes, Compresstome no); construction (Compresstome flimsy, Vibratome solid); chilling capability (Compresstome uses frozen buffer cubes, Vibratome uses ice/dry ice around bath); number of blocks cut simultaneously (Compresstome 1, Vibratome 4).

steps.title: Record Compresstome limitations
steps.instruction: Note that the Compresstome construction is relatively flimsy, lacks a reverse‑blade function, and can jam if the blade contacts the plastic specimen tube, preventing reversal of forward motion.
